note: Not a pudding. Never a pudding. Blackberry jam instead of raspberry, which Bakewell need never know about.
Nettle tea. Tastes green, does you good, and nobody gets stung once it's brewed.
Nettle and elderflower in a proper flask. Mum's own blend. Don't tell the corner shop.
Wild garlic, bruised and bottled. One sniff and anyone's wide awake. Possibly for days.
Flaky pastry round a fruity middle. The money's for the butter.
Nettle twine woven tight and padded with wool. Just like the shop ones, only itchier.
A wicker snare re-bent round hazel. Hedgerow creatures feel right at home in it.
Rowan berries tied with red wool. Gran swore by it. Keeps the Night-folk off.
Scones, cream and hedgerow jam. Jam first. We are in Bath, not Devon, and nobody's fighting about it today.
A proper crimp down the side. The money's for the beef. The mushrooms are for flavour, and for showing off.
A little pot with a seaweed lure. Brook and Tide creatures always have a nose.
A holed stone on a cord, wrapped in weed and glass. Look through it and you see the spirits. They see you too.
A slate-backed lamp with a beeswax wick. Peat to light it. Stone creatures dig harder by it.
Speckled bread: fruit soaked overnight in tea. Butter optional, opinions compulsory.
Oats, cream, honey and a splash of something. The something stays in the cupboard for you.
Sugar, butter, honey, and the dentist's phone number.
A wool thistle on a thorn pin. Wha daur meddle wi' me? Nobody, once they've been stabbed by it.
Tea brack with a ring baked in. Whoever finds it is getting married. Or going to the dentist.
Woven on the first of February, hung over the door. Nothing nasty sticks to whoever carries one.
Three green leaves on a pin. A little luck, a little healing, every single turn.
Sticky oat and ginger cake. Best a week old, which nobody has ever managed.
Sugar, peppermint, and a bit of wild honeycomb. Got people up Everest, so it'll get your lot off the floor.
Stew, but don't call it stew. Mushrooms if the lamb's dear. Red cabbage on the side, or else.
Quartered soda bread on a griddle, with a bit of green through it. Fry it in the morning.
Elderflower cordial, let down with spring water. Clears the head and every ailment going.
An acorn from the Major Oak's own line, polished with truffle oil. Steady as an old tree.
Forged hot on a peat fire with an ammonite set in the crown. Points up, so the luck doesn't run out.
Sea glass wrapped in weed and left on the tideline one night. In the morning, it's a pearl. Don't ask who swapped it.
Oatmeal batter left to bubble, then poured on a hot plate and flipped once. Roll round cheese. Eat warm. Repeat.
